title.narrative: Enhancing the Protection of Girls and Boys through access to safe and quality basic education and integrated GBV prevention and Response in Bade, Geidam and Jakusko LGAs in Yobe State

description.narrative: ltpgt1.ltbgt Enveloped one (1)lt/bgt - ltbgtltugtEducationlt/ugtlt/bgt 70% and ltbgtltugtGender Based Violence (GBV)lt/ugtlt/bgt 30%lt/pgtltpgt2. ltbgtContribution to the Protection of Women and Girlslt/bgtlt/pgtltpgtTo enhance and promote the protection of women and girls, YOPCODI in consortium with AFRYDEV proposes to implement an integrated Education/GBV response in conflict-affected communities in Bade, Geidam, and Jakusko LGAs in Yobe state. The project prioritizes reaching more girls with access to safe, quality, and inclusive basic education services in protective learning environments. The project also seeks to increase awareness and access to coordinated life-saving GBV services including access to information, and skills on menstrual hygiene management to reduce the risk of GBV among women and adolescent girls in formal and nonformal learning centers.lt/pgtltpgtltbgt3. Innovationlt/bgtlt/pgtltpgtltbgta. Digital Literacy Skills for Conflict Affected Children and Adolescents: lt/bgtYOPCODI will through this project provide access to basic digital literacy skills for 200 girls in addition to the regular basic literacy in schools and learning centers. Conflict-affected girls who have passed through previous accelerated education programs and transitioned to formal basic education will be supported and enrolled in digital literacy sessions in the targeted locations. This enables them to acquire the skills necessary to access the Nigeria Learning Passport (NLP) - an interactive and child-friendly digital learning platform developed by UNICEF. This will be in the form of special sessions organized for girls, with dedicated facilitators and monitors ltbrgtto observe compliance and assess learning outcomes regularly. The basic digital literacy sessions will be in cohorts for three months, after which they will be linked to the NLP, thereby expanding access to quality basic education alternatives.lt/pgtltpgtltbgtb. Empowering Mothers for Increased Access to Quality Basic Education:lt/bgt To mitigate regular drop-out of conflict-affected children (especially girls) from formal and non-formal education due to negative social norms or poor socio-economic conditions, the project will support mothers, especially woman-headed households to support and ensure enrolment, attendance, and retention of marginalized and at-risk girls. This will be implemented through improved engagement and awareness of women and girls to participate in education programs as well as train and empower women whose children are at risk of drop-out with micro business start-ups to boost their socio-economic conditions and encourage continued access to quality basic education ltspangtfor girls, mitigate their protection risks and bridge gender equality gaps in access and continuity to education amongst conflict affected population. lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtltbgtc. Integrated School-Related GBV Prevention and Response:lt/bgt This project seeks to address identified gaps in education in emergency response in Yobe State through an innovative approach of blended education-GBV response for conflict-affected boys and girls. Targeted activities will mitigate GBV risks, provide specialized case management services and referral systems for survivors as well as improve awareness through the use of electronic audio devices to enhance access to information on GBV including PSEA reporting and feedback mechanism.lt/pgtltpgtThe 12-month project under the NHF 2023 1st standard allocation will seek to provide 3, 775 conflict-affected children (ltbgtltigt2,452 - 65% Girls and 1,321 - 35% boys)lt/igtlt/bgt opportunities to access and continue learning basic literacy, numeracy, and psychosocial support services. The project will provide teaching and learning materials, construct/rehabilitate temporary learning spaces and classrooms, and train 280 teachers ltbgt(160 F and 120 M)lt/bgt on pedagogy, MHPSS, conflict-sensitive teaching techniques, and GBV prevention and response. Community and other stakeholders will be engaged consistently to promote AAP in education and GBV response. We will also train 300 SBMC Members to support project implementation across target communities. lt/pgtltpgtltbgtThe Overall project target is 19, 130 people.lt/bgtlt/pgt
